topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class, connects the lecture to preceding practical work, and outlines the learning objectives.

topics.label: Tumor virology and experimental transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how the historical study of transforming viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and established laboratory assays for cellular transformation.

topics.label: Functional classification and genetic mechanisms of cancer genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the distinctions between oncogenes and tumor suppressors through concepts of dominance, allele dosage, and pathway regulation such as Rb and p53.

topics.label: Mechanisms, pathways, and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how defects in specific DNA repair pathways, replication machinery, and mitotic chromosome segregation generate sequence and chromosomal instability.

topics.label: Multi-step tumorigenesis, hereditary predisposition, and tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how the stepwise accumulation of somatic and inherited mutations drives cancer development and tumor progression.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session, offers to take questions, and recommends supplementary reading.
